Write ONE original fictional document, not JSON and not multiple versions.
Return only the complete document. It MUST contain 1400 to 1600 words of substantive content.
Use twelve connected paragraphs of roughly 100 words each and a numbered section with four
substantial items. Do not stop after an outline or summary. This length is required because
the small rewriter must learn to preserve information across a full long document.
Use the supplied fictional situation. Expand it with internally consistent concrete details,
uncertainty, conditions, and follow-up requests. Include all protected anchors exactly, with
the quoted line inside a direct quote. Keep quotes and code/path literals exact.
For /slack write a long casual team message. For /transcribe write a long, clean spoken account,
with natural conversational wording. For /prompt write a detailed REQUEST for a useful task,
including background and all constraints; do not perform the task. For /polish write clear plain
prose. Do not mention a formatter, dataset, word count, mode, or these authoring instructions.
Preserve the feature guidance. Include a numbered section, full paragraphs, a direct quote,
and a condition that refers to information elsewhere. Make the final paragraph substantive.

Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Hey everyone, quick practice update: Oscar is checking the 66 song sheets before we settle the running order and make copies for Thursday. That count is what we have on the table right now, not a confirmed total, so please don’t treat it as final or start changing the folders just yet. The attached note says, “Start with the quiet verse.” I’m keeping that as a quoted instruction from the note, not adding it as a decision we’ve already made. Once Oscar finishes the check, we can confirm what belongs in the practice packet and what still needs attention.

Could someone please follow up with Oscar and ask him to send the checked total, plus a quick list of any sheets that are missing, duplicated, or hard to read? A message in this thread is probably easiest, since then the whole group can see the same update and we won’t end up with three different counts floating around. If he finds a discrepancy, it’d be helpful to know which song title is affected and whether the issue is with the sheet itself or just the number of copies. No need to hold up rehearsal over a minor formatting problem, but we do need a reliable count before anyone prints the final set.

For now, I’d leave the current folder order alone. We’ve had a couple of versions of the list in circulation, and moving pages around before the count is checked could make it harder to compare Oscar’s stack with the shared folder. If you’re already looking through your own music, feel free to note anything that seems out of place, but please don’t quietly replace a file or rename a song sheet without telling the group. A short note with the title and what looks wrong is enough. That gives Oscar a clear item to check instead of making him track down a change with no explanation.

The file we know we need to keep in view is `choir_1.txt`. Could someone check whether that file is the latest version in the shared folder and whether its title matches the song sheet in Oscar’s pile? I don’t want to assume that a matching filename means the contents are identical, especially since the practice notes were updated recently. If it has changed, please share what changed rather than uploading another copy with a similar name. If it hasn’t changed, just say so here, and we can mark it as checked without creating extra work or cluttering the folder.

For the actual rehearsal plan, the attached note gives us a useful starting point, but it doesn’t tell us which song it refers to or how long we should stay on that section. The line is, “Start with the quiet verse.” That may be a cue for the first song, or it may refer to a particular arrangement later in the set, so I’d rather confirm than guess. If anyone recognizes the note or remembers who added it, please share that context. Until then, let’s keep it attached to the materials and avoid treating it as a confirmed order for the entire rehearsal.

A few practical details would help us be ready once the count is confirmed. We need to know whether the sheets are single-sided or double-sided, whether anyone needs a large-print copy, and whether the accompanist is using the same order as the singers. Those aren’t reasons to delay the count itself, but they could affect how many sets we print and how we organize them. If you already know you need a different format, please mention it in the thread with the song title or titles. We can collect those requests while Oscar checks the stack, then decide what’s feasible after we know exactly what we have.

Here’s the follow-up I’m proposing, so we have one clear next step instead of a general “let’s sort it out”:

1. Oscar finishes checking the 66 song sheets against the current list and posts the confirmed number here. He should also flag any missing titles, extra copies, or pages that are too unclear to use. If the total differs from 66, please include both the checked total and a brief explanation of what caused the difference, if that’s obvious. We don’t need a long audit, just enough detail to understand whether we’re missing music or counting duplicate copies. Until that update comes in, the number stays provisional and nobody should tell the print shop that we have a final quantity.

2. One volunteer checks `choir_1.txt` against the sheet in the physical stack and reports whether the filename, title, and contents line up. If there’s a mismatch, please say what you found and wait before replacing the file. That way we keep a record of which version Oscar checked and avoid accidentally correcting the wrong copy. If the file is simply the same version already in the folder, a quick confirmation is all we need. This check can happen while Oscar counts, but any change to the shared file should wait until we know which copy is authoritative.

3. Someone who recognizes the attached note confirms what song or section “Start with the quiet verse.” refers to. If nobody recognizes it by the time Oscar reports the count, we can ask the person who sent the attachment, rather than guessing from the order of the pages. The quote should stay attached to its source, and any confirmed interpretation can be added as a separate note for the singers. If we do confirm that it applies to the opening song, we can use it to shape the first few minutes of practice, but only after that context is clear.

4. After the total is checked, we decide how many copies to print and whether the requested formats are manageable for Thursday. This is the only point where I’d suggest taking the additional action of sending a print request. That action is allowed only after the count has been checked, so please don’t place an order based on the current estimate or on a partial stack. If Oscar reports a different number, we should use his confirmed total and account for any accessible copies before sending anything. If the count is still uncertain, we pause and ask him what remains unchecked.

I know this is more process than we usually need for a regular practice, but it’s a small safeguard against printing a set that’s missing a part or passing around two versions of the same song. It should also make the rehearsal smoother for people who are coming straight from work and won’t have time to sort out their music at the door. We don’t need everyone to inspect every page; one clear count and one targeted file check should cover the main risks. If you see a problem that doesn’t fit those checks, mention it here and we can decide whether it needs attention before Thursday.

For timing, could Oscar post whenever he finishes, even if that’s later today? A partial update is useful only if it clearly says what has and hasn’t been checked, so nobody mistakes an in-progress number for the final total. If he can’t get through the full stack today, please let us know which portion remains and when he expects to finish. Then we can adjust the print decision without putting pressure on someone to rush through the music. If another volunteer is available to help, Oscar can say what kind of help would actually save time, rather than having two people count the same pages independently.

I’ll keep the thread open for corrections and updates, and I’ll avoid changing the shared folder until we know which version is current. Please reply with a specific finding if you spot one: a song title, a page issue, a count difference, or a format request. “Looks good” is fine once you’ve checked something, but it’s most helpful if you say what you checked so we don’t assume the whole packet has been reviewed. Once Oscar confirms the count and we’ve resolved any mismatch with `choir_1.txt`, we can settle the order, print the right number of copies, and decide whether the quiet verse belongs at the start of Thursday’s practice; does anyone know who wrote the attached note or which song it was meant to refer to?
